assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the physiology of GLP-1 and turning it into incretin-based therapies has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal benefit signals. Clear mechanism, originality across basic physiology and drug development, and exceptional lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (gut hormone physiology and the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the intestinal and metabolic actions) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible three-person basis. Knudsen's drug-design contribution is industrial and is the main allocation question; the three-laureate cap forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical confirmation, approvals and outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide is contested and I have not independently verified the details.
Whether translational medicinal chemistry (Knudsen) should displace a basic-physiology laureate is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has become a standard tool across brain research and increasingly in cell biology, with early clinical translation in vision restoration. Originality and field-wide impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the demonstration of its use in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth) are both decisive. Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation also matters. Six credited names cannot all be recognised, and any trio omits someone with a credible claim.
assessment.maturity: Method is mature and independently reproduced in thousands of laboratories. Clinical translation is nascent, but the tool's impact does not depend on it.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among the discoverers of the channel and the first neuronal users is genuinely disputed.
Choice of Hegemann and Nagel over Boyden or Bamberg is a judgement call under the three-name limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have created a new class of living therapeutics with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and expansion into autoimmunity. Strong conceptual and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified lymphocytes), Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CARs) and June (4-1BB CAR, first clinical successes) cover the arc. Eshhar-type first-generation CAR concepts are not in the supplied credit list, so the configuration may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up, though toxicity, solid-tumour limits and manufacturing remain open. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR credit may be incomplete in the supplied names.
Long-term durability and safety data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory biology, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer. Conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the decisive pair via the Ire1/Hac1 splicing pathway and the mammalian ATF6 and XBP1 arms. Peter Walter's contribution is central and a two-person prize is a tidy configuration. I recall related contributors such as Kohno and Ron but they are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed for decades and is textbook material. Therapeutic translation is still emerging, which does not weaken the basic discovery.
uncertainties: Unlisted contributors to the mammalian response may be thought to merit credit.
Clinical translation of UPR modulators is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines prevent infection and are producing a measurable fall in cervical precancer and cancer, a direct and large public-health effect from a clear technical innovation.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (the Queensland L1/L2 VLP work and vaccine development) are the plausible trio. Priority disputes with other VLP groups, and commercial development contributions, remain unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Real-world population data show strong effectiveness, with continued follow-up of cancer endpoints. Timely, though the 2008 prize for HPV discovery already touched this area.
uncertainties: Overlapping early VLP work by other groups complicates credit.
Cancer-incidence outcomes are still maturing in vaccinated cohorts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VEGF defined a central mediator of angiogenesis and vascular permeability, and its inhibition produced widely used therapies for neovascular eye disease and cancer. Strong biology and a clear patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Dvorak and Senger (vascular permeability factor) and Ferrara (VEGF cloning, biology and anti-VEGF antibody) represent the decisive contributions, and the VPF and VEGF identity was established jointly. Ferrara is the strongest single claim.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and clinically validated, particularly in ophthalmology; oncology benefits are more modest. Timely.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the VPF and VEGF discoveries is a historical credit question.
Oncology efficacy is limited relative to the ophthalmic effect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition converted CML from a fatal disease into a chronic condition and established the paradigm of targeted oncology, with a very clear causal chain from lesion to therapy.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and biology), Lydon (the chemistry and programme leading to the compound) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are credible. Credit to the originating Rowley and Witte/Baltimore discoveries is outside this candidate and leaves an upstream-credit question. Several honours have already recognised these three.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data are mature and the paradigm is validated. Timely or somewhat late relative to impact.
uncertainties: Upstream cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries make the boundary of the recognised discovery unclear.
Contributions of industry chemists beyond Lydon are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TNF blockade showed that targeting one cytokine can control chronic inflammatory disease, creating a major drug class for rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis. Clear translational logic and large impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini together developed the concept and the clinical proof in rheumatoid arthritis, a coherent two-person configuration. Contributions from the TNF cloning and antibody-engineering communities could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Extensively replicated with decades of use, though biosimilars and newer classes have reduced the novelty. Recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Debate on whether discovery of TNF biology versus its therapeutic use is the recognised achievement.
Others' contributions to the antibody engineering are not in the supplied credit.
